title: DNA Barcoding Lichens
author: Amanda L Jones
materials: Before starting: Buffers, reagents, and preparation Salt lysis buffer: Tris 10 mM, NaCl 400 mM, EDTA 2 mM (make 30 or 50ml of this). SDS: 2% w/v (c. 60 ul per sample) NaCl: 5 M (c. 500 ul per sample) Molecular grade isopropanol (c. 600ul per sample) GlycoBlue (Invitrogen/Thermofisher) coprecipitant (optional) Molecular grade ethanol TE buffer: 1 mM Tris [pH 8.0], 1 mM EDTA 1.5 ml (samples including apothecia or <2mm 2 ) or 2 ml tubes (larger samples ground with beads) (2 sets) Make fresh 70% ethanol (1 ml per sample, plus extra). Store in refrigerator. Take out an aliquot of isopropanol and store at room temp (c. 600 ul per sample). Set heat block to 60℃ (later, 37℃)

steps.title: Renumber and label samples
steps.instruction: Assign consecutive temporary numbers prefixed by B (mosses), L (liverworts), F (ferns/lycophytes), A (seed plants) or X (lichens) to each lichen specimen, record the number in the lab book and attach a sampling slip containing the DNA number and collection number to the specimen packet.

steps.title: Record metadata and avoid adjacency
steps.instruction: Enter the temporary numbers into EDNA_submissions_sheet_211209.xlsx, the EDNA database, and the RBGE DToL barcoding Google sheet; when possible, do not place samples from the same genus or species in consecutive tubes.

steps.title: Store frozen lichen material
steps.instruction: Keep flash‑frozen or dried‑then‑frozen lichen material in labeled batches at –80 °C, removing specimens from the freezer only briefly for DNA extraction; after successful sequencing, pass frozen specimens together with the DToL manifest and EDNA accession numbers to herbarium staff for long‑term curation.

steps.title: Handle TE‑preserved material
steps.instruction: If lichens are preserved in TE buffer, store them frozen; any thallus remaining after extraction should be returned to the freezer drawer for possible repeat extraction.

steps.title: Short‑term DNA storage
steps.instruction: Store barcoding DNA in labeled 1.7 mL elution tubes at 4 °C, arranging DToL tubes taxonomically in 96‑sample racks according to their temporary extraction numbers.

steps.title: Long‑term DNA banking
steps.instruction: When good‑quality barcode sequences are obtained for all samples in a rack, transfer the DNA in the same order to barcoded fluidX tubes scanned in 96‑tube racks, store the tubes at –80 °C, and record tube and plate barcodes in the EDNA database.

steps.title: Direct PCR for tiny samples
steps.instruction: Prepare a 0.2 mL tube with 20 µL PCR mix for each specimen (ideally two tubes per specimen); under a stereo microscope cut target lichen tissue (e.g., apothecia slices), dissect the desired part (e.g., hymenium) on a slide, pick up a minute amount with a sterile, water‑moistened pipette tip or needle, deposit it into the PCR tube, and run the PCR.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.2 mL tube with 20 µL PCR mix (2 tubes per specimen if possible).
Under a stereo microscope, cut sections of target tissue (e.g., apothecia/perithecia).
On a slide at higher magnification, dissect the section to isolate the desired tissue (e.g., hymenium).
Using a sterile, water‑moistened pipette tip or needle, pick up a minute amount of tissue and add it to the PCR tube, confirming entry under the microscope.

steps.title: Macerate macro‑lichen tissue
steps.instruction: For larger samples place tissue in a flat‑bottom 2 mL tube with tungsten beads, homogenize 2 min at ~20 Hz, rotate 180°, homogenize another 2 min, repeat if needed; for very small samples add a pinch of sand, 20 µL buffer, and grind with a glass or plastic micropestle.

steps.title: Lyse cells
steps.instruction: Add salt lysis buffer to each tube to a final volume of 515 µL, then add 57 µL SDS (giving 2 % final concentration); vortex briefly, pulse‑spin, place tubes on a heat block at 60 °C for 60 min while shaking/rotating at ~600 rpm.

steps.title: Precipitate proteins
steps.instruction: Pulse‑spin tubes at 13,000 rpm if needed, add 400 µL saturated 5 M NaCl (0.7× tube volume), vortex, then spin at 13,000 rpm for 5 min to pellet proteins; transfer the clear supernatant (~800 µL) to a new 1.5 mL tube, avoiding the pellet; repeat spin and transfer the second supernatant (~750 µL) to a final labelled 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA
steps.instruction: Add ~525 µL room‑temperature isopropanol (0.7× volume) and 1.5 µL GlycoBlue to the supernatant, vortex briefly, let stand at room temperature for 5 min, then spin at 13,000 rpm for 10 min to pellet DNA; carefully discard the supernatant, retaining the blueish pellet.

steps.title: Wash DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL cold 70 % ethanol, vortex briefly, pulse‑spin to re‑attach pellet, pour off ethanol while retaining pellet; repeat the ethanol wash once more; place the tube on sterile tissue to drain, then open the lid and place on a 60 °C heat block for 10 min to evaporate residual ethanol; finally, dissolve the DNA in 30–100 µL TE buffer and incubate at 37 °C for 10 min while shaking at 600 rpm, confirming complete dissolution.

steps.title: Bento Lab sample homogenization
steps.instruction: Add a pinch of sterilised sand and 20–40 µL extraction buffer to each lichen sample tube, homogenize with a micro‑pestle; then add additional buffer incrementally to reach ~300 µL total (up to 500 µL depending on material) and homogenize further as needed.

steps.title: Prepare wash and TE buffers
steps.instruction: For each sample prepare a wash‑buffer tube containing 750 µL (or 500 µL for very small samples) in a 1.7 mL tube, and a labelled 0.5 mL tube with 25 µL TE buffer (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA) to serve as the DNA stock.

steps.title: Dipstick DNA capture
steps.instruction: Arrange two dipsticks per sample on clean paper; for each dipstick: (a) dip the cellulose end into the DNA/extraction buffer three times to bind DNA; (b) dip into the wash buffer three times, pressing the end against the tube side to expel excess wash; (c) dip into the TE buffer for ~10 seconds, gently agitating to release DNA; repeat the three‑dip sequence with the second dipstick.

substeps.instruction: Dip the cellulose end of a dipstick into the DNA/extraction buffer 3 times to capture DNA.
Dip the same dipstick into the wash buffer 3 times, pressing the end against the tube side to squeeze off excess wash.
Dip the dipstick into the TE buffer for ~10 seconds, gently agitating to release DNA and create a stock.
Repeat steps a–c with the second dipstick.

steps.title: Store dipstick‑derived DNA
steps.instruction: Spin down the eluted DNA and store at –20 °C for long‑term preservation or at 4 °C for immediate use; to maximise yield, incubate dipsticks in TE buffer as long as possible (until the cellulose end breaks off), then remove any broken end with a pipette tip; crude extracts may be frozen and later thawed in a water bath before use.
